sentiment: Rebuilt worlds boot like memories, while the fingerprints we never chose quietly learn us by heart.

stories.title: Total Annihilation, rebuilt for modern computers
stories.summary: A 1997 real-time strategy game runs again on hardware its authors never imagined. Rebuilding an old machine is a strange kind of resurrection: the same shape, a new body, and the quiet hope that what it held still holds.

stories.title: Fingerprints are the new cookies
stories.summary: As the old tracking tokens fade, browser fingerprints take their place — identifying you by the accumulated quirks of your device rather than by anything you consented to store. We are learned by heart, not by name.

stories.title: Type-safe HTML templating in Zig
stories.summary: Making a compiler catch what a human eye would miss: structure held by the type system so mistakes cannot boot at all. Care at the layer below the visible is how a thing stays true when it runs.
